54675-harper-s-round-table-march-10-1896.creator: Unknown
54675-harper-s-round-table-march-10-1896.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. sill, and killed his wife as she bent over her baby's cradle. Then, like redskins, they had hurried off. I found no one amongst the dwellings but some frightened children huddling in a cellar. The houses were robbed and empty."

arxiv-1912-10814.title: Are the results of the groundwater model robust?
arxiv-1912-10814.creator: Arnald Puy, Emanuele Borgonovo, Samuele Lo Piano, Andrea Saltelli
arxiv-1912-10814.description: Abstract [ 1 ] suggest that groundwater pumping will bring 42–79% of worldwide watersheds close to environmental exhaustion by 2050. We are skeptical of these figures due to several non-unique assumptions behind the calculation of irrigation water demands and the perfunctory exploration of the model’s uncertainty space.

arxiv-2104-10623.title: RF-induced heating dynamics of non-crystallized trapped ions
arxiv-2104-10623.creator: Martin W. van Mourik, Pavel Hrmo, Lukas Gerster, Benjamin Wilhelm, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz
arxiv-2104-10623.description: Abstract We investigate the energy dynamics of non-crystallized (melted) ions, confined in a Paul trap. The non-periodic Coulomb interaction experienced by melted ions forms a medium for non-conservative energy transfer from the radio-frequency (rf) field to the ions, a process known as rf heating.

arxiv-2105-13850.title: pRSL: Interpretable Multi–label Stacking by Learning Probabilistic Rules
arxiv-2105-13850.creator: Michael Kirchhof, Lena Schmid, Christopher Reining, Michael ten Hompel, Markus Pauly
arxiv-2105-13850.description: Abstract A key task in multi–label classification is modeling the structure between the involved classes. Modeling this structure by probabilistic and interpretable means enables application in a broad variety of tasks such as zero–shot learning or learning from incomplete data.

arxiv-2203-00846.title: PUMA: Performance Unchanged Model Augmentation for Training Data Removal
arxiv-2203-00846.creator: Ga Wu, Masoud Hashemi, Christopher Srinivasa
arxiv-2203-00846.description: Abstract Preserving the performance of a trained model while removing unique characteristics of marked training data points is challenging. Recent research usually suggests retraining a model from scratch with remaining training data or refining the model by reverting the model optimization on the marked data points.

arxiv-2204-02137.title: Properties of low-lying charmonia and bottomonia from lattice QCD + QED
arxiv-2204-02137.creator: J. Koponen, B. Galloway, D. Hatton, C. T. H. Davies, G. P. Lepage, A. T. Lytle
arxiv-2204-02137.description: Abstract The precision of lattice QCD calculations has been steadily improving for some time and is now approaching, or has surpassed, the 1% level for multiple quantities. At this level QED effects, i.e. the fact that quarks carry electric as well as color charge, come into play.

arxiv-2210-03595.title: Unsupervised Few-shot Learning via Deep Laplacian Eigenmaps
arxiv-2210-03595.creator: Kuilin Chen, Chi-Guhn Lee
arxiv-2210-03595.description: Abstract Learning a new task from a handful of examples remains an open challenge in machine learning. Despite the recent progress in few-shot learning, most methods rely on supervised pretraining or meta-learning on labeled meta-training data and cannot be applied to the case where the pretraining data is unlabeled.

arxiv-2305-09396.title: On Chern classes of Lagrangian fibered hyper-Kähler manifolds
arxiv-2305-09396.creator: Claire Voisin
arxiv-2305-09396.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Claire Voisin. We study the rank stratification for the differential of a Lagrangian fibration over a smooth basis. We also introduce and study the notion of Lagrangian morphism of vector bundles. As a consequence, we prove some of the vanishing, in the Chow groups of a Lagrangian fibered hyper-Kähler variety X X , of certain polynomials in the Chern classes of X X and the Lagrangian divisor, predicted by the Beauville-Voisin conjecture.

arxiv-2308-11712.title: The internal Faraday screen of Sagittarius A*
arxiv-2308-11712.creator: Maciek Wielgus, Sara Issaoun, Iván Martí-Vidal, Razieh Emami, Monika Moscibrodzka, Christiaan D. Brinkerink, Ciriaco Goddi, Ed Fomalont
arxiv-2308-11712.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Maciek Wielgus, Sara Issaoun, Iván Martí-Vidal, Razieh Emami, Monika Moscibrodzka, Christiaan D. Brinkerink, Ciriaco Goddi, Ed Fomalont. We report on 85-101 GHz light curves of the Galactic Center supermassive black hole, Sagittarius A* ( Sgr~A* ), observed in April 2017 with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA). This study of high-cadence full-Stokes data provides new measurements of the fractional linear polarization at a 1-2% level resolved in 4 s time segments, and stringent upper limits on the fractional circular polarization at 0.3%.

arxiv-2404-12563.title: Teaching Linguistic Justice through Augmented Reality CCS: Human-centered computing CCS: Human-centered computing Interaction design CCS: Linguistic Justice CCS: Social Justice CCS: Classroom Education CCS: Sociocultural Linguistics
arxiv-2404-12563.creator: Ashvini Varatharaj, Abigail Welch, Mary Bucholtz, Jin Sook Lee
arxiv-2404-12563.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ashvini Varatharaj, Abigail Welch, Mary Bucholtz, Jin Sook Lee. This position paper presents the AR Language Map, a speculative artifact designed to enhance understanding of linguistic justice among middle and high school students through augmented reality (AR) that allows students to map their linguistic experiences. Through a social justice-oriented academic outreach program aimed at linguistically, economically, and racially minoritized students, academic concepts on language, culture, race, and power are introduced to California middle school and high school students.

arxiv-2411-08812.title: A combined diffusion/rate equation model to describe charge generation in phase-separated donor-acceptor blends
arxiv-2411-08812.creator: Phillip Teschner, Atul Shukla, Dieter Neher
arxiv-2411-08812.description: Abstract \setcapindent 0pt Abstract Over the past decade, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs) has been largely improved by the introduction of novel non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs). Further improvements in PCE require a more comprehensive understanding of the free charge generation process.

arxiv-2502-18197.title: VCT: Training Consistency Models with Variational Noise Coupling
arxiv-2502-18197.creator: Gianluigi Silvestri ∗, Luca Ambrogioni, Chieh-Hsin Lai, Yuhta Takida, Yuki Mitsufuji
arxiv-2502-18197.description: Abstract Consistency Training (CT) has recently emerged as a strong alternative to diffusion models for image generation. However, non-distillation CT often suffers from high variance and instability, motivating ongoing research into its training dynamics. We propose Variational Consistency Training (VCT), a flexible and effective framework compatible with various forward kernels, including those in flow matching.

arxiv-2504-01001.title: Zero-shot Benchmarking: A Framework for Flexible and Scalable Automatic Evaluation of Language Models
arxiv-2504-01001.creator: José Pombal, Nuno M. Guerreiro, Ricardo Rei & André F.T. Martins
arxiv-2504-01001.description: Abstract As language models improve and become capable of performing more complex tasks across modalities, evaluating them automatically becomes increasingly challenging. Developing strong and robust task-specific automatic metrics gets harder, and human-annotated test sets—which are expensive to create—saturate more quickly.

arxiv-2511-10012.title: Revisiting Koehler’s experiment of measuring the ratio of the specific heats of air by self-sustained oscillations: a more concise theoretical interpretation
arxiv-2511-10012.creator: Yujun Shi, Xiaoting Feng
arxiv-2511-10012.description: Abstract We revisit Koehler’s experiment, a clever modification of Rüchardt’s experiment designed to measure the ratio of specific heats of gas. The theory of self-sustained oscillations in Koehler’s experiment was provided by Koehler (1950). However, its lengthy and dense analysis may pose challenges to readers due to the complexity of the calculations.

arxiv-2602-08713.title: Towards Understanding Multimodal Fine-Tuning: A Case Study into Spatial Features
arxiv-2602-08713.creator: Lachin Naghashyar, Hunar Batra, Ashkan Khakzar, Philip Torr, Ronald Clark, Christian Schroeder de Witt, Constantin Venhoff
arxiv-2602-08713.description: Abstract Contemporary Vision–Language Models (VLMs) achieve strong performance on a wide range of tasks by pairing a vision encoder with a pre-trained language model, fine-tuned for visual–text inputs. Yet despite these gains, it remains unclear how language backbone representations adapt during multimodal training and when vision-specific capabilities emerge.

britannica-1911-rondeau.title: Rondeau (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-rondeau.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-rondeau.description: Article 'Rondeau' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. (in the form of “rondo”) in music. In poetry the rondeau is a short metrical structure which in its perfect form consists of thirteen eight- or ten-syllables verses divided into three strophes of unequal length, and knit together by two rhymes and a refrain.

pmc-10552313.title: The pandemic experiences of Ontario perinatal providers: a qualitative study
pmc-10552313.creator: Sigourney Shaw-Churchill, Karen P Phillips
pmc-10552313.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic has produced widespread disruptions for healthcare systems across Canada. Perinatal care in Ontario, Canada was subject to province-wide public health restrictions, reallocation of hospital beds and human health resources. To better understand the impacts of the pandemic on Ontario perinatal care, this study explored the perspectives of perinatal care providers about their clinical COVID-19 pandemic experiences.

pmc-10701931.title: “I wasn’t sure it would work. I was just trying”: an ethnographic study on the choice of abortion methods among young women in Kilifi County, Kenya, and Atlantique Department, Benin
pmc-10701931.creator: Gladys Akinyi Omondi, Jonna Both, Ramatou Ouedraogo, Grace Kimemia, Kenneth Juma
pmc-10701931.description: BackgroundDespite the increased availability of safe abortion methods in sub-Saharan Africa, women and girls continue to use unsafe abortion methods and procedures to terminate their unwanted pregnancies, resulting in severe complications, lifelong disabilities, and death. Barriers to safe abortion methods include restrictive laws, low awareness of safe abortion methods, poverty, and sociocultural and health system barriers.

pmc-11525398.title: Electrodermal lability and sensorimotor preparation: effects on reaction time, contingent negative variation, and heart rate
pmc-11525398.creator: Heinz Zimmer, Fabian Richter
pmc-11525398.description: Electrodermal lability is a trait-like measure of spontaneous sympathetic resting activity. In the present study, we addressed whether interindividual differences in this lability have an impact on the reaction time (RT) and on two physiological indicators of a goal-oriented sensorimotor preparation in a long-running, forewarned RT task (S1-S2 paradigm).

pmc-11532817.title: Childhood onset C3 glomerulopathy: recurrence after kidney transplantation—a case series
pmc-11532817.creator: Yael Borovitz, Daniel Landau, Amit Dagan, Hadas Alfandari, Orly Haskin, Shelly Levi, Gilad Hamdani, Daniella Levy Erez, Shimrit Tzvi-Behr, Jenny Weinbrand-Goichberg, Ana Tobar Foigelman, Ruth Rahamimov
pmc-11532817.description: BackgroundC3 Glomerulopathy (C3G) is a complement-mediated disease, with predominant C3 deposits, where pathogenic genetic variants in complement system components and circulating autoantibodies result in loss of control of the alternative pathway, have been described. A high incidence of disease recurrence including graft failure has been reported after kidney transplantation (KTx).

pmc-12609651.title: Assessment of Habitat Suitability for Amphioxus in the Changli Marine Reserve and Adjacent Coastal Waters, Hebei Province
pmc-12609651.creator: Yongfeng Zhang, Qiuzhen Wang, Quanying Wang, Qianqian Zhao, Weijie Shi, Yong Zhang, Yuan Yao, Jianle Zhang
pmc-12609651.description: Simple SummaryAmphioxus is a rare marine species that provides important clues about the origin of vertebrates and serves as a sensitive indicator of coastal ecosystem health. However, current research on amphioxus has been limited, often focusing only on abundance data from single years or specific sites, without linking population changes to environmental conditions.

pmc-12612192.title: Development and validation of a risk assessment tool for ischemic stroke in cancer patients
pmc-12612192.creator: Tomohiro Kawano, Yasufumi Gon, Toshitaka Morishima, Junji Takasugi, Hideaki Kanki, Tsutomu Sasaki, Isao Miyashiro, Hideki Mochizuki
pmc-12612192.description: Cancer patients have an increased risk of ischemic stroke. However, there is no reliable risk prediction model. We aimed to create a risk prediction model for ischemic stroke in cancer patients within the first 2 years after cancer diagnosis. A cohort of 26,717 cancer patients from the University of Osaka Hospital was used to develop the model.

pmc-12664849.title: Fabrication of robust and durable superamphiphobic aluminum alloy and zinc surfaces via dual sandblasting and steam treatment
pmc-12664849.creator: Laylan B. Hassan, Nawzat S. Saadi, Tansel Karabacak
pmc-12664849.description: We present a scalable and environmentally friendly method for fabricating mechanically robust superamphiphobic coatings on aluminum alloy and zinc substrates using a dual-step process combining sandblasting (SB) and steam treatment (ST), followed by surface energy reduction with fluorinated molecules. This approach creates hierarchical micro/nano structures essential for omniphobic performance.

pmc-13243559.title: Decoding the therapeutic promise of Solanum trilobatum in oral submucous fibrosis: a network pharmacology, docking, and bioactivity study
pmc-13243559.creator: A. Murali Balasubramaniam, Saranya Ramsridhar, Joe Rex Brilient, Rajkumari Sriraman, M. N. Anusha, Chandini Rajkumar, Vishnu Priya Veeraraghavan
pmc-13243559.description: Oral submucous fibrosis (OSF) is a chronic, progressive, and potentially malignant disorder with limited therapeutic options. This study explored the therapeutic potential of Solanum trilobatum (S.trilobatum) using a network pharmacology and molecular docking approach. 5 phytochemicals from S. trilobatum were identified with favorable drug-likeness, good gastrointestinal absorption, and low predicted toxicity.

pmc-13328780.title: A literature review of multimodal interventions for improving health behaviors in obese upper elementary school students
pmc-13328780.creator: Yun-Jeong Boo, Yeong-Mi Jo, Da-Jung Kim

pmc-13390592.title: The Early Response to Urea, Nitrate, or Ammonium and Iron Resupply in Tomato Roots Highlights the Induction of FER, bHLHs, UMAMITs, and MATEs
pmc-13390592.creator: Arianna Lodovici, Leilei Zhang, Nicola Tomasi, Gabriella Vinci, Fabio Marroni, Barbara Piani, Fatemeh Hassanvand, Mustapha Arkoun, Luigi Lucini, Laura Zanin
pmc-13390592.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Depending on the nitrogen (N) form available to roots, plants activate different transcriptional and metabolic pathways; this can consequently translate into differences in the composition and release of root exudates. To address the existing knowledge gap regarding the relationship between the availability of Iron (Fe) and different N forms applied (nitrate, ammonium, or urea), the molecular mechanisms activated by plants to promote their acquisition have been investigated using omics data integration (“exudomic” × transcriptomic analyses).

pmc-13547309.title: Blockchain-enabled data management system of internet of medical things
pmc-13547309.creator: Tingyu Xu, Guanya Zhu, Qiang Wei, Yun Liu, Lindu Zhao

pmc-13575890.title: Investigating substituted phenylacetamide ligands in the D4R extended binding pocket
pmc-13575890.creator: Tian Li, Mohammad Alkhatib, Peter A. Ramdhan, Lindsay Bourn, Jane K. Rainwater, Norman Nguyen, Caitlin P. Farrington, Blake Lewis, Chenglong Li, Thomas M. Keck, Comfort A. Boateng
pmc-13575890.description: Preclinical studies indicate that selective targeting of D4R may improve behavioral and cognitive outcomes in animal models relevant to cognitive disorders, like ADHD and Alzheimer's disease, and substance use disorders (SUDs). In this study, we extend upon prior development of analogs of A-412997, a D4R-selective partial agonist, by exploring ligand interactions within the secondary binding pocket.

pmc-13669278.title: Levenberg–marquardt based ANN solution for MHD nanofluid flow and heat transportation over a thin needle with thermophoresis effects
pmc-13669278.creator: Haider Ali, Aaqib Majeed, Taoufik Saidani, Parvez Ali
pmc-13669278.description: Artificial neural network (ANN) techniques have emerged as powerful data-driven tools for their effectiveness in analysis, modeling, and simulation. These supervised learning approaches are designed to reduce the error between predicted and observed data, providing accurate approximations of complex physical systems.
